finding: The 180-day automated re-evaluation adds no detection value in the model. Hybrid expected false negatives (1.749 per 1k charities) are identical to Continuous monitoring alone (1.749). The extra cost (+$1.8k per 1k charities; +$17.7k at 10k) buys only the policy flag meets_180_day_validity. The vetting comparison also ignores OA-CHR-002, the transaction-time status check at approval and release, which already catches published revocations at the moment of exposure.
evidence: Beneficium.fs Hybrid uses window=latencySrc and miss=min(autoMiss,humanMiss), the same detection terms as Continuous; staleShare is set to 0 by assertion, not by modelled detection. OA-CHR-002 runs 2.0 per grant (DETERMINISTIC).
proposed_correction: Model the 180-day step as a control with its own detection term: share of stale-source charities x probability that fresh evidence is obtained. Credit the transaction-time check in pFn. If the step only re-reads the same sources, record it as ECHELON-POLICY with zero risk reduction, and let the owner decide on Continuous plus grant-time check plus targeted refresh of stale-source charities.
estimated_impact: Vetting choice may move to Continuous plus targeted refresh, saving about $18k/yr at 10k active charities and $180k at 100k. The control claim changes more than the money.

finding: False-negative exposure counts the publication-lag window (source_latency_days 45) as taxable-distribution exposure. Under Rev. Proc. 2018-32, sponsoring organizations generally may rely on IRS Tax Exempt Organization Search and BMF status until a revocation is published, unless they had knowledge or were responsible. Grants made before publication therefore carry little 4966 exposure. In the Continuous and Hybrid cases about 98% of modelled pFn comes from that latency term.
evidence: pFn = inel x (window + miss x cycle)/365, where window = 45 d and miss x cycle = 0.02 x 30 = 0.6 d. Rev. Proc. 2018-32 (IRB 2018-23) consolidated Rev. Proc. 2011-33; IRS DAF reliance page. Verified via search 2026-11-27.
proposed_correction: Split ineligibility events into IRS revocations (exposure begins at publication) and non-IRS adverse events (dissolution, fraud, sanctions, state AG action; exposure begins at the event). Apply the 4966 cost only to the post-publication and non-reliance share.
estimated_impact: Expected false-negative cost falls by roughly 50-90% for the Continuous and Hybrid rows (about $44k to $5-20k at 10k charities). Small in absolute terms, but it reverses the stated rationale for periodic review.

finding: A single cost per false negative ($2.5k base, labelled as the 20% 4966 tax) mixes the wrong mechanics. The 4966 first-tier tax is abatable under IRC 4962 for reasonable cause and correction, because 4962(b) includes subchapter G, which overstates routine cases. At the same time it understates the tail: a grant to a sanctioned or terror-linked charity (OFAC strict civil liability), or a fraud charity with press exposure. The fund-manager 5% tax (cap $10k) under 4966(a)(2) is also not separated.
evidence: IRC 4962(b) text on law.cornell.edu (qualified first tier tax includes subchapters A, C, D or G, except 4941(a)), fetched 2026-11-27. CO-016 notes OFAC strict liability.
proposed_correction: Use two or three event classes: routine revoked or dissolved recipient (abatable; recovery labour, typically under $1k); disqualified recipient with no abatement (20% x grant); sanctions or fraud tail (low probability, $50k-$500k incl. counsel and voluntary self-disclosure). Report expected value and P95 separately.
estimated_impact: Expected value roughly unchanged. P95 tail of $100k+ should appear in stress and insurance sizing.

target: Beneficium compliance_rate BNP-041 vs roles.csv compliance fractional rate
finding: Vetting labour is costed at $67.69/h (BNP-041). The staffing model buys the same compliance hours at $190/h x 1.1 availability premium = $209/h. Vetting-alternative labour is therefore understated about 3x relative to how the headline model actually pays for compliance work.
evidence: vetting-alternatives.csv: 500 h -> $33,845 (=$67.69/h). headline-staffing COMPLIANCE: 794 h -> $165.9k (=$209/h).
proposed_correction: Use one compliance rate source across Beneficium and staffing, either the marginal pool rate or an explicit dedicated-hire rate.
estimated_impact: Human-review-heavy alternatives rise about 3x in labour. For example, Full manual review at 10k charities goes from $338k to about $1.0M. The ranking is unchanged; the gap between Hybrid and manual widens.

finding: The compliance pool has one named person and no backup, at every scale shown. CO-018 itself specifies a backup approver for sanctions dispositions with a same-day to 2-business-day SLA. The same person is the OFAC compliance officer, the eligibility-exception adjudicator and the 4966 remediation owner. One absence stalls payment release on any potential match. Key-person and segregation-of-duties failure.
evidence: Staffing.fs: | "COMPLIANCE" | "COMM" -> 1.0. results.md section 4: COMPLIANCE named persons 1 at 93.2% simulated utilisation. CO-018 coverage: 'backup approver'.
proposed_correction: Set min_named for COMPLIANCE to 2 (the backup may be a sponsor compliance officer under documented delegation, or an external sanctions specialist on retainer). Add a backup retainer.
estimated_impact: +40-80 h/yr retainer, about $8-17k/yr.

target: Staffing.fs fractional/dedicated decision; roles compliance dedicate_threshold 0.6
finding: The model chooses fractional compliance at $209/h even where a dedicated hire is clearly cheaper. At $500M, 794 h costs $165.9k fractional, against $121.8k for a 1.0 FTE dedicated compliance analyst, who also gives continuous ownership. The 0.6 FTE dedicate threshold is not cost-based: break-even is about 0.40 FTE at these rates. Over-costed in that direction.
evidence: results.md section 4: COMPLIANCE 794 h, fractional, $165.9k. roles.csv compliance dedicated base $121,842, fractional $190 x premium 1.1. Productive hours about 1,462.
proposed_correction: Select the mode by minimum cost (with hire_step 0.5 allowed), not a fixed FTE threshold. Keep a fractional senior or counsel layer for judgment calls.
estimated_impact: About -$35k to -$45k/yr at $100M-$500M AUA in the compliance pool (net of finding ADV-CS-005 backup).

finding: Segregation of duties is modelled only as a head count in the OPS, AUTH and FINANCE pools. The dominant fraud and integrity risk in a 2-3-engineer organisation is engineering privileged access. Engineers who can read and write production data, payee bank details or the generated ACH/positive-pay files can bypass every application-level dual control. The founder is simultaneously owner, executive, engineer and approver. No independent (non-engineering) review of privileged sessions, database changes or payment-file integrity is costed. SOC 1 ITGC testing will focus here.
evidence: echelon-shared notes section 7 item 5 ('One human holds every role'). OA-TEC-017 covers tenant-data access requests only. No activity for independent review of break-glass and privileged logs, or file hash and control-total confirmation outside engineering.
proposed_correction: Add controls and costs: (1) just-in-time privileged access with session logging (about $3-10k/yr tooling); (2) weekly review of privileged-access and database-change logs by the compliance owner or sponsor (2 h/week, about 100 h/yr); (3) payment-file control totals and hash independently confirmed by the sponsor in the bank portal before release; (4) founder excluded from approving his own production changes.
estimated_impact: About $20-35k/yr plus a sponsor-borne review of 1-2 h/week. Removes a likely SOC 1 exception.

target: OA-TEC-001; roles engineering min_fraction 'named security/on-call owner'; results ENG 2 dedicated + founder
finding: On-call is priced as 19.6 min/day of review, staffed by 2 dedicated engineers plus a founder with a 400 h cap. If any 24x7 response commitment is made, each engineer is on call for about 26 weeks a year, with no stipend, no follow-the-sun coverage and no cover for absence. That is not sustainable and is a retention risk. Conversely, 24x7 human response is not legally required: grants are not time-critical intraday if payment release fails closed.
evidence: OA-TEC-001 minutes 19.6, 365/yr. original-cost-trace-notes lists '24x7 on-call for payment release' at $30-150k (UNKNOWN). ZBP-016 founder 400 h.
proposed_correction: Make an explicit owner decision: business-hours support plus extended December and bank-cutoff windows, fail-closed release and automatic pause, after-hours best effort. Price an on-call stipend (about $5-10k per engineer per year) or an MSP/MDR after-hours tier. Do not sell a 24x7 RTO SLA at 2-3 engineers.
estimated_impact: +$10-40k/yr depending on the SLA chosen. A 24x7 contractual SLA would need 4+ people, about +1-2 FTE ($212-425k).

finding: Detection tooling is underfunded. FC-010 ($3k) covers SAST and dependency scanning only. There is no SIEM or managed detection and response, no endpoint detection, device management or phishing-resistant MFA for workforce devices, and security monitoring is 55 h/yr of triage. SOC 2 CC6/CC7 and cyber underwriters (MFA, EDR and backup attestations) expect these. With 2-3 engineers, MDR is the only realistic route to out-of-hours detection.
evidence: FC-010 $0-12k 'dependency and code scanning; secrets scanning'. OA-TEC-003 365 x 0.3 x 30 min. infrastructure-notes lists 'Security tooling, SIEM' as excluded.
proposed_correction: Add a line: MDR/SIEM-lite (cloud-native alerting plus MDR vendor) $15-40k/yr; endpoint detection, device management and hardware keys about $1-2k per person per year.

finding: The named security owner is budgeted at 100 h/yr, a fraction of an engineer, with no security specialist anywhere in the model. That one person also owns the written information security program under 201 CMR 17, pen-test remediation, vendor security reviews, incident command and quarterly reports to the audit committee. For a platform preparing payment files for multiple sponsors this is thin. Institutional due-diligence questionnaires ask for a named CISO or vCISO.
evidence: CO-052 effort 100 h/yr. CO-050 40 h/yr. OA-COM-002/003 due-diligence questionnaires.
proposed_correction: Budget a fractional vCISO at 150-250 h/yr ($200-275/h), or explicitly assign and train one of the engineers with protected time (about 0.15 FTE).

finding: The cost of a breach or incident beyond labour is unpriced. A security incident costs 24 engineering hours plus 8 ops hours. Forensics beyond the $5k retainer, breach counsel, notification and credit monitoring, sponsor indemnities, and the insurance retention or deductible ($10-50k typical) are all missing. The vendor's statutory duty is usually to notify the data owner (the sponsor), but the MSA will shift resident-notification costs to the vendor. A breach-counsel retainer is mentioned in control-obligations-notes but not priced.
evidence: parameters ZBP-025 24 h, ZBP-026 8 h. FC-013 $5k. control-obligations-notes line 123 'breach-counsel retainer'. No retained-loss or expected-loss line.
proposed_correction: Add expected retained loss: P(notifiable breach) 2-5%/yr x (retention $25k + uninsured items such as betterment, lost revenue and contractual credits, $25-75k), plus a breach-counsel panel through the insurer. Add a stress scenario: one breach of 50k records at about $150-250 per record gross, with insurer limits tested.
estimated_impact: Expected value +$2-6k/yr. Tail $1-10M gross; at $1M limits this becomes an existential uninsured exposure.

finding: Insurance is priced at $1M-type limits with no quote: cyber $15k, E&O $12k, crime $8k. Institutional sponsors and ODFIs commonly require $3-5M technology E&O and cyber, plus crime with third-party (client property) and funds-transfer-fraud or social-engineering coverage. On the other side, tech E&O and cyber are usually written as one combined policy, so two separate premiums may double-count base fees. Insurers also need a formed entity; the licensor LLC is not formed.
evidence: fixed-costs FC-001..003 ASSUMPTION/low, 'No quote'. echelon-shared notes section 7 item 4 (Echelon Foundry, LLC not formed).
proposed_correction: Price a combined tech E&O and cyber policy at $3-5M ($25-60k), crime with a third-party and social-engineering endorsement ($8-20k), and D&O if outside investors or board ($5-15k). Obtain broker indications before relying on them.
estimated_impact: Net about +$10-50k/yr over $35k base.

target: fixed-costs FC-005 activation vendor_controls; configurations CFG-1/2/6
finding: SOC 1 is activated only where the vendor runs controls (CFG-3/4/5/7). In CFG-1, CFG-2 and CFG-6 the platform is still the sponsor's fund ledger, fee and NAV calculator, reconciliation engine and payment-file generator. Its automated application controls and ITGCs are relevant to the sponsor's financial statements whoever performs the manual steps (AU-C 402). Sponsor auditors will request a SOC 1 or perform their own testing at higher sponsor cost. Licensing-only configurations look $44.5k plus 120 h cheaper than they are.
evidence: configurations.csv vendor_runs_controls=N for CFG-1, CFG-2, CFG-6. CO-043 cites AU-C 402.
proposed_correction: Activate SOC 1 for every configuration in which the platform is the system of record, possibly with a reduced scope. Alternatively, model a per-sponsor user-auditor testing cost borne by sponsors.
estimated_impact: +$44.5k plus about 120 h prep (about $18-25k) per year in CFG-1, CFG-2 and CFG-6; break-even rises about $35-60M AUA at 20 bps.

finding: SOC 1 and SOC 2 are priced as independent engagements ($72k combined), alongside a 50%-allocated shared assurance programme ($45k). One firm performing both examinations over a common ITGC control set normally discounts the second report and shares testing. Some evidence collection in FC-105 overlaps OA-TEC-020 (80 h of SOC evidence support).
proposed_correction: Price a bundled SOC 1 plus SOC 2 engagement (about 15-25% lower) and remove the overlap between FC-105 and OA-TEC-020 evidence hours.
estimated_impact: About -$10-20k/yr.

target: CO-022 OFAC independent testing; CO-027 Nacha audit; FC-007; owner direction DF-ASR-2026-0D0F
finding: Independent testing of the sanctions programme is costed as 16 internal hours. With a single fractional compliance owner, nobody is 'independent of the audited activities'. In addition, owner direction DF-ASR-2026-0D0F authorizes no independent-review spend, which conflicts with the SOC, pen-test, Nacha-audit and OFAC-testing lines in the model. The Nacha audit fee ($15k) is likely high: payments associations commonly perform TPSP Rules Compliance Audits for less, and the requirement to audit by December 31 does not mandate a CPA.
evidence: CO-022 citation: OFAC Framework, Testing and Auditing. echelon-shared notes section 8 (DF-ASR-2026-0D0F). Nacha 'ACH Rules Compliance Audit Requirements' (Article One 1.2.2; consolidated 2019).
proposed_correction: Fold OFAC programme testing into the external Nacha audit or the SOC scope (an incremental $3-8k), or use the sponsor's internal audit. Reprice the Nacha audit at $5-10k. Record the conflict with the owner direction as a blocking decision rather than a cost assumption.
estimated_impact: OFAC testing +$3-8k; Nacha audit -$5-10k. Net about zero. Governance conflict unresolved.

target: OA-CMP-001 sanctions alert rate (exception 0.0009 per screening)
finding: The sanctions alert rate of 0.09% of screenings (about 23 alerts/yr at 2,000 accounts) is optimistic for fuzzy name screening of donors, successors and thousands of charity names, especially with delta re-screening on every list update. The alert workload may be several times higher until match rules are tuned. The driver also counts screenings per account only, not per active charity or payor.
evidence: OA-CMP-001: 12.5 per_account, exception 0.0009, 25 min. CO-018 'about 50 alerts at 15 min, ASSUMPTION'.
proposed_correction: Use 0.3-1% in the first year, falling to 0.1-0.3% after tuning. Add a per-active-charity screening driver. Validate in a pilot against the actual list vendor.
estimated_impact: +50-300 h/yr, about $10-60k/yr at fractional compliance rates (less if dedicated).

finding: Only TPSP status is modelled. If Unbound transmits files to the ODFI under its own agreement, or for several sponsors through one channel, it becomes a Third-Party Sender. A TPS takes on warranty and indemnity liability for its Originators' entries, an annual risk assessment it cannot delegate (CO-028), ODFI underwriting and exposure limits, and Nacha registration through the ODFI. That changes capital, insurance and legal cost materially. The model has no switch for this.
evidence: CO-028 effort '16 hours/year if TPS' with no activation in the model. Nacha 'Third Parties in the ACH Network'.
proposed_correction: Make 'no TPS' a design invariant: the sponsor is the Originator, files are released through the sponsor's ODFI credentials, and Unbound has no ODFI agreement. Otherwise add a TPS scenario (risk assessment, higher crime and E&O limits, return-liability reserve and counsel).
estimated_impact: If TPS: +$20-60k/yr plus contingent return and unauthorized-entry liability. If designed out: no cost, but needs counsel and ODFI confirmation (CO-026).

finding: Disaster recovery in the default C1 deployment depends on same-region, provider-managed database backups (free up to provisioned size, locally redundant by default). These sit in the same tenant and subscription that a compromised admin credential or ransomware actor could delete. No immutable or cross-account backup and no geo-redundant backup is priced. Ten-year OFAC and recordkeeping retention (CO-020, CO-015) and the sponsor's books depend on it.
evidence: infrastructure-notes: 'Backup storage is free up to 100% of provisioned storage'. Geo-redundant blobs priced only in C2. OA-TEC-006 DR drills 2 x 40 h assume something to fail over to.
proposed_correction: In C1 add geo-redundant database backup, an immutable or locked vault or logically air-gapped copy in a separate subscription with separate admins, and quarterly restore-to-alternate-region tests. A warm region (C2) can stay optional.
estimated_impact: Infrastructure +$50-300/mo (about $1-4k/yr). It removes an unrecoverable-loss scenario.

target: Deployment C2 warm DR region; CO-060
finding: Not over-engineered as stated, but worth confirming as a cost_down: a warm DR region is not legally required. A regional outage delays grants by hours to days, which creates no 4966 or Nacha breach, and contribution timing for donor deductions is fixed by the donor's transfer, not by platform posting. The real continuity control is CO-060, under which the sponsor can approve and pay through its own bank channel and see verified balances if the vendor fails. That should be drilled (8 h/yr is light) rather than met with a second region.
evidence: CO-060 coverage 'Annual continuity drill, 8 hours/year'. C2 adds about $2.4k/yr on Azure.
proposed_correction: Keep C2 optional and sold as a contractual add-on. Fund a sponsor-side manual payment fallback drill (about 16-24 h/yr across vendor and sponsor) and a documented export of balances and payees refreshed daily to the sponsor.
estimated_impact: C2 avoided (-$2.4k/yr); fallback drill +$2-4k/yr.

target: Key-person: founder; ZBP-016; min_named_engineering met by founder
finding: Key-person risk is acknowledged but not costed or mitigated. The founder is the third engineer used to meet author-plus-two, the commercial lead, contract owner and in practice the security owner, with 400 h/yr spread across about 30 initiatives. Sponsors' vendor-risk processes will require source-code and data escrow, documented runbooks, succession, and possibly key-person insurance. Losing the founder leaves the platform without a qualified change approver and with no one able to sign SOC management assertions.
evidence: echelon-shared notes section 6-7 ('One human holds every role'; 30 initiatives). headline-staffing ENG named 3 = 2 dedicated + founder.
proposed_correction: Add source-code and data escrow ($3-8k/yr), key-person life and disability cover ($2-5k), and runbook and succession documentation hours (40 h/yr). Treat 'standalone without founder' (CFG-7) as needing a third paid engineer or reviewer, not a 40 h retainer.
estimated_impact: +$5-15k/yr fixed. CFG-7 at small scale could need about +0.5 FTE engineering (+$100k) if the change-approval rule is kept.

finding: Two non-author approvers for control-relevant changes is ECHELON-POLICY (CNV-PLT-010), not a SOC 1 or SOC 2 requirement. Auditors accept one independent, competent reviewer plus automated controls (protected branches, signed builds, CI tests, separate deployment pipeline permission). The rule creates a hard 3-engineer floor, which is the model's main reason to involve the founder or a retainer. The parameter is labelled VERIFIED-FACT/high, but it only verifies that the policy exists, not that it is needed.
evidence: parameters ZBP-043 'author + two non-author approvers', evidence_class VERIFIED-FACT. CO-047 mandate_class ECHELON-POLICY. echelon-shared notes: 'hard staffing requirement'.
proposed_correction: Offer author-plus-one, with a second approver only for payment-file, ledger-posting and authority modules, as a policy alternative. Relabel ZBP-043 as a policy choice (ASSUMPTION/owner decision).
estimated_impact: Lowers the engineering floor from 3 to 2 named persons. About -$6-10k/yr retainer in the founder-led view; avoids about 0.5 FTE in standalone (CFG-7) at low scale.

finding: Security incidents are modelled twice, inconsistently. Activity OA-TEC-004 gives 4 incidents/yr x 25 h (100 h), and incidentSpecs separately adds 1 incident/yr x 24 h engineering plus 8 h ops. The basis for each is unstated, and the headline claim of '1 security incident/yr' is not what the model actually charges.
evidence: operational-activities OA-TEC-004: 4 per_platform x 1500 min. Analysis.fs incidentSpecs uses inc_security_rate=1, inc_security_hours=24.
proposed_correction: Keep one source: either a severity mix (e.g. 4 minor at 8 h and 0.5 major at 120 h incl. ops) or the activity row. Document which is used.
estimated_impact: About ±24-40 engineering hours (±$4-6k). Mainly a clarity fix.

target: CO-030 Nacha data security; CO-049 GLBA
finding: Two citations are applied too broadly in one direction and too narrowly in the other. CO-030 (Nacha supplementing data security) applies only above 2M ACH entries a year; Unbound volume is far below that, so the obligation is contractual or good practice, not Nacha-mandated, although SOC 2 requires the same encryption anyway. CO-049 dismisses GLBA because the nonprofit sponsor is outside FTC jurisdiction. But Echelon Foundry is a for-profit entity within FTC jurisdiction, and whether it is itself a 'financial institution' processing financial data is not analysed.
evidence: CO-030 limitations ('security requirement >2M transactions'). CO-049 citation (FTC Act 15 USC 44 'corporation' = for profit).
proposed_correction: Reclassify CO-030 as RISK-BASED/CONTRACTUAL below threshold. Add the vendor-side GLBA question to the counsel list. If it applies, the Safeguards Rule requires a Qualified Individual, annual board report and FTC notice within 30 days for events affecting 500+ consumers, largely satisfied by the 201 CMR 17 program.
estimated_impact: Under $5k/yr either way. Legal-classification accuracy only.
